title: Rollout risk cartography and heatmap
content:
Notes to self: mapping release risks to observable signals, mitigations, and cohort rules. Goal: make decisions deterministic during ramp and avoid fuzzy heuristics. 

Context:
- Target: staged rollout for hosted text-generation v2.3.0 engine changes (KV cache eviction tweak + kernel selector fallback). Small perf win but potential regressive behavior for long-context prompts.
- Launch window: 2025-11-12 to 2025-11-20 (quiet window nights PST).
- Strategy: 4-stage canary with anchored fallback model (v2.2-stable) and traffic steering by client affinity.

Assumptions:
- Prefix KV cache improvements should reduce tail latency for medium tokens but may increase OOM risk for long sequences on shared instances.
- Most customer impact will be visible in 99th latency, OOM traces, and a subtle semantic drift for very long prompts (>2048 tokens).

Risk cartography (quick):
- Risk: latent semantic regression for very long prompts
  - Signals: sudden spike in eval regression score on benchmark set; customer bug reports with >2048 tokens; increased semantic-similarity drop (>0.06 cosine on eval set).
  - Threshold: regression delta >= 0.05 on daily eval (rolling 6h) or >3 customer incidents in 12h
  - Immediate mitigation: route affected clients to fallback model; pause rollout and open high-pri incident; start targeted replay of failing inputs.

- Risk: increased 5/10/25xx OOMs on long-context flows
  - Signals: instance OOM count, pod restarts labeled oom_kill, new gcore dumps, RL3 errors in SRE channel
  - Threshold: >2 OOMs per shard in 1h or >0.5% of requests hitting OOMs in any one region
  - Mitigation: reduce batch sizes for the variant pool; enable forced quantization fallback; divert traffic fraction to dedicated nodes with higher-memory SKUs.

- Risk: 99p latency regressions (bad for real-time partners)
  - Signals: token-level latency 99th percentile increases >25% vs baseline; RU cost spike for affected routes
  - Threshold: sustained >25% increase for 30m on key customer routes OR >40% across global traffic for 15m
  - Mitigation: auto-fallback to v2.2-stable for high-latency cohorts; scale up burst capacity; temporarily disable batching optimization for small sequences.

Heatmap (decision guidance):
- X axis = probability (low/medium/high), Y axis = impact (low/medium/high).
- High impact & high probability = immediate halt + full rollback
- High impact & medium probability = pause + targeted rollback for affected cohorts + canary expansion freeze
- Medium impact & high probability = throttled ramp + additional telemetry sampling
- Low impact & low probability = continue ramp, add extra monitoring and post-rollout eval.

Cohort selection heuristics (practical):
- Seed cohort 1 (0.1%): internal dev keys + canary orgs (hard-coded allowlist).
- Cohort 2 (1%): hashed client_id mod 1000 in [0..9] excluding enterprise contracts with SLA. Example pseudo-SQL: SELECT client_id WHERE abs(hash(client_id)) % 1000 < 10 AND contract_tier != 'enterprise'.
- Cohort 3 (5%): mod 100 in [0..4], prefer low-latency client regions (us-west/us-east).
- Cohort 4 (gradual): expand by doubling fraction every 4 hours if all green for last 60 min and no threshold hits.

Model pinning notes (temp strategy):
- Do NOT change customer pinned model configs. For rollout, create a parallel routing rule: if route in canary cohort -> serve v2.3-canary else serve pinned version. This preserves customer expectations and avoids accidental version drift.
- KV cache considerations: cache keys include model version and compilation fingerprint; when switching cohorts ensure TTL for cache entries is short (5m) to avoid cross-contamination during first 2h.

Preflight checklist (quick run):
- [ ] Smoke: end-to-end smoke on dev cluster with long-context (>4k tokens) synthetic prompts
- [ ] Regression eval: run eval set (n=12k long prompts) and compare similarity metrics; produce report
- [ ] SRE capacity check: confirm spare_shards >= 2 per region and burst capacity available
- [ ] Observability: dashboards for 50/90/99 latency, OOMs, error_code distribution, unit-cost per route all wired to alerting
- [ ] Canary keys: seed list verified + rollout gating policy created in Console with pinned fallback targets
- [ ] Client comms: scheduled note to top-10 customers and partner Slack channel

Rollback decision matrix (simplified):
- Immediate rollback if any of:
  - Regression delta >= 0.07 on semantic eval within 6h
  - OOMs > 3 per shard in 1h OR any widespread data loss/garbage-corruption alerts
  - Any persistent 99p latency >2x baseline for >30m on enterprise routes
- Soft pause + targeted mitigation if:
  - 99p latency 25-100% increase on non-enterprise routes OR increasing tail errors <0.5%

Telemetry queries (bookmarks):
- Latency rollup per model: SELECT model_version, route, percentile(99, latency_ms) FROM token_logs WHERE timeframe = last_30m GROUP BY model_version, route
- OOMs: SELECT count(*) FROM instance_events WHERE event_type = 'oom_kill' AND timeframe = last_60m GROUP BY region, shard
- Semantic drift: run embedding similarity job: compare embeddings(old_model, new_model) -> aggregate mean cosine delta by prompt_bucket

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- Divert 10% of route foo to fallback: curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/route-update -d '{"route":"foo","cohort_rule":"hash(client_id)%100<10","target_model":"v2.2-stable","fraction":0.10}' 
  (note: replace with Console UI flow in prod)
- Force immediate cache eviction on canary nodes: ssh to canary-hosts && sudo /opt/redwood/bin/evict-cache --age 300

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to validate semantic regression quickly at scale? Need lightweight online eval that samples production requests and computes similarity without leaking PII. Possible approach: hashed-sample + local embedding computation + differential stats.
- Do we want a temporary auto-abort rule when x% of routes hit user-facing error 5xx? Need product input.
- Confirm cost model: if fallback to dedicated nodes occurs, who owns incremental spend? Need finance sign-off for >$5k/day.

Notes to self: keep rollout small, instrument the noisy signals first (OOM, 99p latency) and sanity-check semantic metrics asynchronously. Prefer freeze-and-probe over blind expansion.

Reference snippets and where to paste: put SQL bookmarks in Metrics > Saved Queries, copy curl templates to Console quick-commands.

Signed-off-by: hannah. Quick follow-ups: Rafael will confirm Canary org list by 2025-11-05; Priya to run the eval job and post the diff by 2025-11-08.
